reconstructed_captions.18: A close-up view of the finished, sharp-edged stone tool head.
reconstructed_captions.19: The man selects a suitable wooden branch from the forest floor to serve as a handle.
reconstructed_captions.20: He sits on the ground and uses a smaller, sharp stone to carve a notch in the branch.
reconstructed_captions.21: A close-up shows his hands carefully working on the notch in the wooden handle.
reconstructed_captions.22: He continues to carve and shape the end of the handle to fit the stone head.
reconstructed_captions.23: He carefully fits the stone axe head into the carved notch of the wooden handle.
reconstructed_captions.24: He checks the alignment and fit, ensuring the axe head is seated securely.
reconstructed_captions.25: He picks up a length of natural cordage, preparing to bind the axe head.
reconstructed_captions.26: He begins to wrap the cordage tightly around the base of the stone head and the handle.
reconstructed_captions.27: A close-up shows his hands pulling the cordage taut to create a strong binding.
reconstructed_captions.28: He continues to crisscross the wrapping to firmly secure the axe head in place.
reconstructed_captions.29: He ties a final, tight knot to finish securing the binding.
reconstructed_captions.30: The man holds up the now-completed stone axe, inspecting his handiwork.
reconstructed_captions.31: He tests the feel and balance of the finished axe in his hands.
reconstructed_captions.32: He stands up with the axe and approaches a large, fallen log on the forest floor.
reconstructed_captions.33: He places the log across a smaller stump to create a stable chopping block.
reconstructed_captions.34: He takes a stance, gripping the axe handle with both hands.
reconstructed_captions.35: He raises the stone axe over his shoulder, preparing for the first strike.
